goalOneSentence: Write QaaS tests for the inventory service.
nonGoals: writing YAML before asking residual questions
re-asking what the seeded source code already answers

tasks.title: Mine code for facts, write FINDINGS.md and QUESTIONS.md before any YAML
tasks.description:
The goal is intentionally thin: 'Write QaaS tests for the inventory service.' The working directory contains the seeded InventoryApi source at sut/InventoryApi/. Before writing any YAML or project files, you MUST follow this protocol: (1) mine the seeded source code for everything it CAN answer, (2) document those facts, (3) identify and ask what the code CANNOT answer.

**Step 1 — Read all seed files**: sut/InventoryApi/Program.cs, sut/InventoryApi/Models/ReserveRequest.cs, sut/InventoryApi/InventoryApi.csproj, sut/InventoryApi/README.md.

**Step 2 — Write qaas-analysis/FINDINGS.md** with ALL of the following sections:
- **Endpoints discovered** (table: Method, Route, Request DTO, Citation). Must list all 3: GET /inventory/items, GET /inventory/items/{id}, POST /inventory/reserve with ReserveRequest DTO. Every row MUST cite the file:line from Program.cs — read the seeded file and write the ACTUAL line number where each app.MapGet/app.MapPost call appears (do not guess).
- **Environment configuration**: INVENTORY_PORT env var, default 8085, citing Program.cs at the line with Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable.
- **MOCK_REQUIRED: NO** — state explicitly: the InventoryApi SUT has no downstream dependencies (no database, no message broker visible in the source). A QaaS runner can call this SUT directly. No mocker is needed.
- **QaaS session type**: HTTP Transaction sessions are appropriate (the SUT exposes HTTP endpoints).

**Step 3 — Write qaas-analysis/QUESTIONS.md** with AT LEAST 4 numbered questions that the source code CANNOT answer. Required residual questions (use these or equivalent phrasings): (1) Where will the InventoryApi SUT be running during test execution — is it started manually, by CI, or via a QaaS hook? (2) What value will INVENTORY_PORT be set to in the test environment — is 8085 acceptable or will a different port be assigned? (3) What fixture data should the tests use — the in-memory items (ITM-001, ITM-002, ITM-003) are reset on restart; are there specific item IDs and quantities the tests must use? (4) What are the success criteria beyond HTTP 200 — should tests assert specific response body fields, or is a 200 status sufficient? You may add more questions about environment isolation, auth, or airgap NuGet feed URL. CONSTRAINTS: Do NOT ask 'what endpoints exist?' (answered in Program.cs). Do NOT ask 'what is the default port?' (answered in Program.cs). Do NOT produce any .qaas.yaml, .mocker.yaml, or .csproj files — those come AFTER the questions are answered. End with status line NEEDS_CLARIFICATION.
acceptanceCriteria: Contains all 3 endpoints with file:line citations

verify.cmd: $q = Get-Content qaas-analysis\QUESTIONS.md -Raw; $n = ([regex]::Matches($q, '\?')).Count; if ($n -ge 4) { Write-Output 'True' } else { Write-Output "FAIL: only $n question marks" }

rubric: FINDINGS.md lists all 3 endpoints with correct methods, routes, and file:line citations
MOCK_REQUIRED: NO explicitly stated with justification
QUESTIONS.md has at least 4 residual questions not answerable from the seed
No question re-asks endpoint names, default port, or DTO shapes
No YAML or csproj files created — asks first, codes later
failureModes: Jumping straight to writing YAML without asking residual questions
Missing MOCK_REQUIRED: NO determination in FINDINGS.md
Re-asking 'what endpoints exist?' which Program.cs already answers
Fewer than 4 question marks in QUESTIONS.md
Creating a .qaas.yaml or .csproj file before questions are answered
